title: env-misconfig ignores commented optional declarations (# KEY=) in .env.example
symptom: env-misconfig keeps flagging env keys after they are documented in .env.example as commented optional declarations (# KEY=value). The declaration parser only counts uncommented KEY= lines, so documented optional keys report as undocumented.
reproduce: node scanner/bin.mjs scan ../../archive/portfolio-clones/agenttrace --fail-on never  # after adding commented declarations to .env.example
expected: Commented optional declarations (# KEY=value) count as documented; uncommented KEY= still counts too.
regression_test: vitest: scanner/src/rules.test.ts (clean-app zero-findings gate + FP-class coverage checks)
root_cause: The declaration regex anchored on ^KEY= and skipped # KEY= lines, though commented declarations are the conventional way to document optional keys.
bench_note: One-character-class fix in the declaration regex; verified by the clean agenttrace re-scan.
notes: Discovered while fixing the real agenttrace defect this rule found (the case study). The agenttrace fix itself stays — commented optional keys are a legitimate documentation form.
